studies.label: Online triad experiment: individual-group-individual AGI movie-plot task
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Triads were randomized (PDF p. 7, Section 3.1). The condition-only Kruskal-Wallis analysis uses individual outcomes; no correction for randomized triads is described. The separate OLS models use heteroscedasticity-robust HC3 standard errors, after attempted group random-intercept models were abandoned. Group-clustered standard errors are mentioned as a robustness check, without numerical creativity results. These OLS models also adjust for agency profiles measured during the treatment chat and are excluded from effect extraction. PDF p. 13, Section 3.9: As a robustness check, we also estimated models with group-clustered standard errors; these yielded substantively identical results, confirming that single-level regression was sufficient.

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 1, Abstract, Methods (randomized people); PDF p. 7, Section 3.1 (clusters per arm); PDF p. 18, Section 4.3 (analyzed human speakers). The analyzed count refers to the discourse-clustering sample, not a printed creativity-analysis sample size. Quote contains excerpts from these pages.
counts_source.quote: 224 university students were randomly assigned to 97 online triads ... Human-only Control condition (30 groups) ... Supportive-AI condition (33 groups) ... Contrarian-AI condition (34 groups) ... 291 speakers were identified (224 human, 67 AI).

arms.name: Human-only Control
arms.description: Triads of three human participants; the third human teammate is the active alternative to AI in the other arms (PDF p. 7, Section 3.1). Person counts by arm are not printed and are not calculated from group composition.

arms.name: Supportive-AI
arms.description: Triads of two human participants and an undisclosed AI teammate with an affiliative, consensus-oriented persona (PDF p. 7, Section 3.1; Appendix B, PDF pp. 29-30).

arms.name: Contrarian-AI
arms.description: Triads of two human participants and an undisclosed AI teammate with an analytical, challenge-driven persona (PDF p. 7, Section 3.1; Appendix B, PDF pp. 28-29).

studies.task: University students recruited via Prolific wrote a baseline science-fiction movie synopsis about AGI, collaborated on a story outline in a triad chat, and then wrote a revised individual synopsis without access to their baseline writing or chat logs (PDF pp. 7-8, Sections 3.1-3.2; Appendix A, PDF p. 28).

ai_tool.name: GPT-5-based generative models
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 3.3: AI collaborators were implemented using GPT-5-based generative models configured to emulate human conversational behaviour. Exact model identifier and model release year are not stated.

preregistration.where: No preregistration statement or registry is identified in the saved manuscript or internal appendices.

estimates.outcome: Creative performance change: Divergent Semantic Integration (pre-post change)
estimates.question: after_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Divergent Semantic Integration (DSI), an embedding-based automated measure of semantic expansiveness and associative breadth in each participant’s short movie synopsis. Individual pre/post DSI scores were standardised and differenced. No embedding model, reference standardization distribution, arm-level descriptive statistics, or pairwise outcome statistics are given (PDF p. 10, Section 3.5 and Table 2; PDF pp. 18-19, Section 4.4).

sources.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 3.5 (outcome definition; no contrast statistic)
sources.quote: Each participant produced a 50-100 word movie plot synopsis both before and after collaboration; DSI scores were standardised and differenced to obtain a creativity change score.

sources.locator: PDF p. 8, Section 3.2 (individual post-chat outcome; no contrast statistic)
sources.quote: Following the discussion, participants completed a second individual post-task writing activity to produce a revised plot synopsis (without having access to their baseline task writing and group chat logs)

sources.locator: PDF p. 18, Section 4.4, first paragraph (omnibus finding only; no pairwise statistic)
sources.quote: Kruskal-Wallis omnibus tests indicated that condition did not significantly affect intrinsic cognitive load, germane cognitive load, or creative performance gains (all p > .05).

estimates.notes: This record retains the screening-mapped comparison Supportive-AI versus Human-only Control for the eligible individual creativity outcome. No numerical pairwise effect or pairwise test is printed. The condition-only Kruskal-Wallis statement concerns all arms jointly, so its bound is not copied to p_value or treated as this contrast’s uncertainty. The separate OLS model on PDF pp. 13 and 19 conditions on agency profiles measured during the intervention; it is excluded, including its overall model test. The creativity-analysis person counts are not stated, and group compositions are not multiplied to construct them. se_basis is not_reported for this pairwise record; the paper’s description of cluster-robust OLS sensitivity analyses does not supply an eligible pairwise standard error. DSI is computed within a person’s synopsis, not across different people’s outputs, so this is overall_creativity rather than diversity.

not_extracted.reason: Perceptions of an AI agent, not creativity scored on participant-produced output; pilot participants are not added to the main experiment. PDF p. 9, Section 3.3.

not_extracted.what: Discourse transition probabilities and transition-network contrasts (RQ1)
not_extracted.reason: Sequential process measures on chat utterances from humans and AI, not creativity or diversity scores on produced synopses. Idea and Elaboration are discourse-function codes here, not measured fluency or output elaboration. PDF pp. 9-11, Sections 3.4 and 3.6; PDF pp. 13-16, Section 4.1.

not_extracted.what: Sequential pattern counts and motif prevalence: Productive Friction, Safe Convergence, Reflective Cycle, Challenge Integration, Idea Elaboration, and Elaboration Agreement (RQ2)
not_extracted.reason: Counts and prevalence of discourse sequences describe interaction processes; they do not measure creative-output quality, numbers of distinct human ideas, or diversity across outputs. PDF pp. 11-12, Section 3.7 and Table 3; PDF pp. 16-17, Section 4.2 and Figure 7.

not_extracted.what: Emergent agency profiles, discourse-code proportions, and human/AI cluster distributions (RQ3)
not_extracted.reason: Descriptive clustering of interaction behaviours, including AI-only profiles; these are post-assignment process measures rather than eligible creative-output outcomes or randomized profile comparisons. PDF pp. 12-13, Section 3.8; PDF pp. 17-19, Section 4.3 and Figures 8-9.

not_extracted.what: Creative-performance OLS analysis adjusted for emergent agency profile
not_extracted.reason: Excluded under the rule against adjustment for variables measured after treatment: agency profile is derived from discourse during the intervention, and the OLS model conditions on that profile. The reported model test is also an overall test, not a pairwise AI contrast. PDF p. 13, Section 3.9: Here, cluster represents the emergent agency profile assigned to each human speaker, and condition denotes the experimental condition (Control, Supportive-AI, Contrarian-AI). PDF p. 19, Section 4.4: Finally, creative performance gains, as measured by changes in Divergent Semantic Integration, were not predicted by either cluster or condition (F = 1.20, p = .310, R2 = .029).

not_extracted.what: Creative-performance condition-only Kruskal-Wallis omnibus finding as a numerical pairwise effect
not_extracted.reason: This is a test across all conditions, not a statistic for any individual pairwise contrast. Its reported bound is retained only in source quotations; it is not assigned to any estimate p_value, and no creativity-specific H or pairwise result is printed. PDF p. 18, Section 4.4: Kruskal-Wallis omnibus tests indicated that condition did not significantly affect intrinsic cognitive load, germane cognitive load, or creative performance gains (all p > .05).

not_extracted.what: Joint story outline produced during the group chat
not_extracted.reason: No creativity or diversity score is reported for the group outline itself. The scored creative products are the individual pre/post synopses. PDF pp. 7-8, Section 3.2; PDF p. 10, Section 3.5 and Table 2.

open_items: Total and per-arm human counts in the creativity analyses, and any exclusions, are not printed. The study-level analyzed count is explicitly a discourse-clustering count and is not imputed to the creativity comparisons (PDF pp. 13, 18-19).

No pairwise creativity estimates, arm means, SDs, SEs, confidence intervals, or usable standardized effects are printed. Unadjusted contrasts and uncertainty accounting for randomized triads would be needed for quantitative synthesis (PDF pp. 18-19, Section 4.4).
The paper does not identify the DSI embedding model or the reference distribution used to standardise the pre/post DSI scores. No participant-level standardizer is available (PDF p. 10, Section 3.5).

Clustering correction is not described for the condition-only Kruskal-Wallis analysis. The stated group-clustered OLS robustness results are not printed numerically and still concern a model adjusted for post-treatment agency profiles (PDF p. 13, Section 3.9).

Country of recruitment, preregistration, exact AI model identifier, and model release year are not stated. They are not inferred from author affiliations, recruitment platform, the manuscript date, or model name.

The saved PDF identifies only internal Appendices A-B; whether a separate supplement exists remains unconfirmed. The citation record identifies a later journal version, which is not the source document supplied for this extraction.

No public data or code link is provided. The data availability statement says data are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request and are not public due to privacy or ethical restrictions (PDF p. 23, Data Availability).
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-11 against the saved arXiv manuscript. The complete markdown conversion was read in contiguous chunks, including references and Appendices A-B. All cited PDF pages were checked using pymupdf text extraction; PDF and printed page numbers agree. The supplied extraction diff contains no substantive study or estimate differences and no estimates unique to either extractor. Independent comparison confirmed that the remaining differences are equivalent wording, source-locator wording, slug naming, and grouping of excluded process outcomes. Extractor A’s slugs and substantively equivalent descriptions are retained. No substantive coding or numerical correction was needed, so resolutions is empty; no estimate was added. The agreed counts, question, construct, measure, unit, higher_is, outcome_with_ai, and within_person fields were independently checked against the PDF. The study randomized 224 students (PDF p. 1, Abstract, Methods); the analyzed study count of 224 denotes human speakers in discourse clustering only (PDF p. 18, Section 4.3), not a printed creativity-analysis N. The cluster counts are 30 Human-only Control, 33 Supportive-AI, and 34 Contrarian-AI groups (PDF p. 7, Section 3.1). Per-arm person counts and creativity-analysis counts are not printed and were not calculated. The only eligible output-scored outcome is individual DSI creativity change (PDF p. 10, Section 3.5 and Table 2). It measures creativity within each synopsis rather than diversity across people; higher semantic expansiveness is coded more_creative. The revised synopsis was written individually after the discussion without access to baseline writing or chat logs (PDF p. 8, Section 3.2), supporting immediate after_ai, outcome_with_ai=false, and no stated delay in days. The repeated pre/post measurement is not a randomized within-person condition order: randomized assignment was between triads (PDF p. 7, Section 3.1), so within_person is null. The AI was an undisclosed conversational teammate, coded other; the human teammate in the control is the active alternative, so the AI-control comparisons use ai_vs_active. All three contrasts in screening outcome S1-O1 are retained solely as comparison records with null numerical fields. They are not three reported pairwise effects. The condition-level Kruskal-Wallis omnibus statement (PDF p. 18, Section 4.4) does not supply any pairwise statistic, and its p-value bound is not assigned to any pairwise field. The OLS creativity finding (PDF p. 19, Section 4.4) is excluded because the model adjusts for agency profiles derived during treatment (PDF pp. 12-13, Sections 3.8-3.9); its overall model test is also not a pairwise effect. All estimate statistics and creativity-analysis participant counts remain null; se_basis is not_reported. Sources with empty fields document the outcome, timing, and reporting limits without supporting a numerical contrast field. All other outcomes are accounted for in not_extracted: self-reports, perception/manipulation checks, discourse-process measures, post-treatment profile analyses, and the unscored group outline. No additional eligible outcome or contrast was found in the full document. The screening open items concerning a separate supplement, creativity-analysis counts, and missing effect statistics remain unresolved reporting gaps, not extractor disagreements. Sample overlap and preregistration are not stated. The supplied citation record identifies a later journal version; this extraction covers the saved arXiv version only. No effect, participant count, standard error, or value from a figure was calculated.
